subject: Retention & backup carve-outs — DPA redlines and e-sign flow
messages:
From: Emma Soto <esoto@acmecloud.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial DPA asks — retention / backups / DR carve-outs

Hi Vivek / Laura,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier. The procurement & security teams at AcmeCloud ran the proposed DPA and flagged three items we need clarified before we can move to signature:

1) Backups / DR retention: Our compliance team needs an explicit carve-out that allows us to retain encrypted backups for up to 180 days for forensic and recovery purposes.
2) Subprocessors: We need the current subprocessors list and confirmation you notify us 30 days before adding any that process EU customer data.
3) Cross-border transfers: Can you confirm the mechanism you rely on (SCCs, BCRs, or adequacy)?

I've attached a short note with our requested language and a tracking spreadsheet of the systems that would be in scope (Acme_DPA_requests.pdf).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the 180-day backup carve-out and how you prefer to execute (DocuSign or AdobeSign)? We aim to close this before our renewal on May 1.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call if easier.

Best,
Emma Soto
Sr. Contracts Manager
AcmeCloud, Inc.

--
Attachment: Acme_DPA_requests.pdf (summary of asks)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Soto <esoto@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA asks — retention / backups / DR carve-outs

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Neha (legal) and Laura (security) so we can get a concise response and proposed redline.

Quick answers up front:
- Execution: we prefer DocuSign but can accommodate AdobeSign if your vendor requires it.
- Subprocessors: we'll share the current list and commit to 30-day notice for new vendors that process EU data; we typically publish a CSV with processor name, region, and purpose.

On the backup retention ask: Redwood's standard position is to allow encrypted backups retained for a limited period strictly for disaster recovery and restore operations. We don't keep operational copies beyond restoration windows. I want Neha to propose specific language — my inclination is to propose a compromise of 120 days rather than 180 given data minimization principles, while allowing an exception for narrow audit logs if necessary.

Next steps: Neha — can you provide a redline and suggested clause text by tomorrow? Emma — if you can share any regulatory justification for 180 days (e.g., audit or legal hold reasons), that'll help.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

--
(Attachment referenced: Redwood_DPA_template.docx — will upload to shared Drive)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-16T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: proposed retention/redline (for Acme)

Vivek / Laura — drafted suggested language below and attached a short text file with the exact redline snippets for insertion into the DPA (Suggested_retention_clause.txt). High level: aim for a pragmatic compromise that addresses Acme's recovery needs while limiting retention scope.

Proposed retention carve-out (summary):
- Accept encrypted backup retention up to 120 days for disaster recovery and restoration only.
- Backups are immutable and stored encrypted; access limited to on-call ops for restores and legal requests.
- On termination, Redwood will stop creating backups and will securely delete or overwrite backups within 120 days except for narrow audit/log artifacts retained up to 365 days where legally required.

Clause snippet (suggested):
"""
Backup and Disaster Recovery. Notwithstanding Section X (Data Deletion), Provider may retain encrypted backups and disaster recovery copies containing Customer Personal Data solely for the purpose of network and service restoration, for a period not to exceed one hundred twenty (120) days following creation. Such backups will be subject to Provider's access controls and encryption practices and will not be used for any other operational purpose. Upon termination of the Agreement, Provider will cease generation of backups for Customer data and will delete or render irretrievable Customer Personal Data in backups within one hundred twenty (120) days, except that Provider may retain limited audit or logging records required by applicable law for up to three hundred sixty-five (365) days.
"""

Other items:
- Subprocessors: we will provide the CSV (Subprocessors_2026-04-15.csv) and commit to 30-day notice for processors that will handle EU data; for cross-border transfers we rely on the EU SCCs + our Data Processing Addendum; we can add explicit language referencing SCCs.
- E-sign: Redwood uses DocuSign standardly; ask Acme to accept DocuSign envelopes. If they insist on AdobeSign, legal can coordinate a one-off process.

I'll attach the redline snippets to this thread; recommend sending the redline in Drive and then issuing a DocuSign envelope for signature.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: Suggested_retention_clause.txt (redline snippet)

From: Emma Soto <esoto@acmecloud.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-17T08:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: proposed retention/redline (for Acme)

Neha / Vivek — thanks for the quick turnaround and the suggested text. A couple of clarifications from Acme's side: 

- We can accept the 120-day compromise for backups generally.
- Our audit team still requires that certain security/event logs may be retained up to 365 days for incident investigation; this would be restricted to logs that are necessary for security incident response and compliance.
- Please confirm that the logs retained to 365 days will be accessible only to named roles and cannot be used for profiling or other operational uses.

We're comfortable with DocuSign. I've prepared an envelope and can send once you confirm the final redline in Drive. Sending the envelope link here: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/EXAMPLE-ENVELOPE-ID (DocuSign_envelope_stub.link).

If you can confirm subprocessors CSV and the SCC reference language, we'll accept and sign the DPA.

Thanks,
Emma Soto
Sr. Contracts Manager
AcmeCloud, Inc.

--
(Attachment: none; DocuSign envelope link provided)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Soto <esoto@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-20T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention & backup carve-outs — DPA redlines and e-sign flow

Emma — great, thank you. Confirming and next steps: 

1) Retention: Redwood accepts 120 days for encrypted backups (DR/restore only). We accept a limited carve-out for security/event logs up to 365 days for incident investigation and compliance, with strict access controls (only named security/ops roles) and contractual prohibition on use for profiling or product analytics.

2) Subprocessors: attached is the current list (Subprocessors_2026-04-15.csv) — includes hosting providers, telemetry pipeline processor, and managed database provider. We commit to 30 days' notice for any new subprocessor that will process EU personal data and to update the CSV on the shared Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/AcmeCloud/DPA-redlines

3) Transfers: Redwood relies on EU SCCs (Module II / Module III where applicable) as the transfer mechanism; we'll insert an explicit SCC reference into the DPA redline.

4) E-sign: DocuSign is fine. I'll review the Drive redline right now and ask Legal to initial/approve. Once we confirm, we will complete the DocuSign envelope. Please send the envelope to legal@redwood.ai and to my attention.

I'll attach the working redline (Redline_DPA_v2.docx) and the subprocessors CSV; once signed we'll upload the fully executed PDF to the shared Drive.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

--
